title: The Overlooked Shot That Protects Newborns From Uncontrolled Bleeding
hook: Newborns are naturally short on a vitamin their blood needs to clot — and a growing number of parents are skipping the shot that fixes it.
key_points: Newborns are naturally low on vitamin K, leaving them vulnerable to vitamin K deficiency bleeding (VKDB), which can be fatal, including bleeding in the brain.
A single prophylactic vitamin K shot at birth has been recommended worldwide for more than 50 years to prevent this.
More parents have been refusing the shot in recent years — in Sweden, refusal rates climbed from 0.66% in 2006 to 1.5% in 2021.
A 2026 JAMA Pediatrics study found infants who skipped the shot had significantly higher risk of bleeding, including in the brain.
Investigators say the government lacks comprehensive data on how many newborns get the shot, making preventable bleeding cases hard to count.
content_html: Every newborn is naturally short on one vitamin their blood needs to clot properly — which is why, for more than 50 years, doctors worldwide have recommended a single shot of vitamin K right after birth.
extra_html: Without it, infants face a real risk of vitamin K deficiency bleeding (VKDB), a condition that can cause uncontrolled bleeding, including inside the brain, and can be fatal if untreated. Despite the shot's long safety record, more parents have been refusing it in recent years — in Sweden, the refusal rate climbed from 0.66% in 2006 to 1.5% in 2021. The stakes of that choice were underlined by a 2026 JAMA Pediatrics study, which found that infants who skipped the shot had a significantly higher risk of bleeding, including in the brain. Compounding the problem, an investigation found that the government lacks comprehensive data on vitamin K uptake, making it hard to know how many preventable infant bleeding cases — and deaths — are going uncounted; U.S. lawmakers have since called on the CDC to start tracking rates for this routine newborn procedure.

flashcards.prompt: Why are newborns specifically at risk of vitamin K deficiency bleeding?
flashcards.back_html: Newborns are naturally low on vitamin K, a nutrient their blood needs to clot properly, leaving them vulnerable to uncontrolled bleeding, including in the brain, if untreated.

flashcards.prompt: What did the 2026 JAMA Pediatrics study find about infants who skipped the vitamin K shot?

choices.text: They had a significantly higher risk of bleeding, including in the brain
They showed no difference in bleeding risk compared to those who got the shot
They had a lower risk of bleeding but more allergic reactions

flashcards.explanation_html: The study found a clear, significantly elevated bleeding risk — including intracranial bleeding — in infants who didn't receive the shot.

flashcards.prompt: What data gap is complicating efforts to understand this problem?
flashcards.back_html: The government lacks comprehensive data on how many newborns actually receive the vitamin K shot, making it hard to know how many preventable bleeding cases go uncounted.
